clue.text: Outspoken writer given discharge without penalty

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so the writer's name is taken by how it sounds rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: Sir Walter Scott, the Scottish novelist
to discharge a prisoner is to free them

explanation.surface: A plain-talking author is let off without punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' looks like a description of the writer's manner but signals a homophone: SCOTT said aloud gives SCOT. SCOT-FREE means escaping without paying a penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting off scot-free means escaping without any punishment or cost.

clue.text: Rebuke old-fashioned vet

parts.note: to check someone is to rebuke or restrain them
something out is no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a vet for being behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to inspect or examine it, a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Pleasing impression of beginning to work

parts.note: taking as an adjective means attractive, charming
an effect is the impression something makes

explanation.surface: Making a nice impression as you start a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule or drug that is coming into force or starting to act is said to be operative from that moment.

clue.text: Humorous exchange of notes about standard English

indicators.note: the two notes go about, i.e. surround, the word for standard

parts.note: re, the second note of the sol-fa scale
te, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
par is the standard or normal level

explanation.surface: Witty banter about correct English usage.
explanation.walkthrough: Sol-fa is the do-re-mi singing scale; the single word 'notes' supplies two of its syllables, and 'about' wraps them round the golfing standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Repartee is quick, witty conversation or retort, a back-and-forth of clever remarks.

clue.text: Kinky corsets for the Guards?

indicators.note: kinky in the sense of twisted, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Unusual underwear issued to a regiment of soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guards' looks like the regiment but is a verb or plural noun: those who accompany and protect; the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Escorts are people who accompany others for protection, as guards do.

clue.text: Naval manoeuvre involving many a destroyer

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or involve, the extra letter
a manoeuvre moves things about, so these letters are repositioned

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, a crossword standard for many

explanation.surface: A naval exercise featuring a number of warships called destroyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' rearranges NAVAL to VANAL, and 'involving' puts D inside it. 'destroyer' tempts you towards ships, but here it is a person who wrecks things.
explanation.definitionFit: A vandal is someone who wilfully damages or wrecks property.

clue.text: Lion, in play, is well-enclosed

definitions.meaning: in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.definitionFit: A snug place is cosy and tightly enclosed; Snug is also the character who plays Lion in Shakespeare.

clue.text: The early variety has to be tough

indicators.note: a variety of the words means a different arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: An early strain of plant must be hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Leathery meat is hard and chewy, tough like hide.

clue.text: Remove unwanted products from forage

definitions.meaning: in engineering, to ... a cylinder is to clear out its burnt gases
to search about for food or useful items

explanation.definitionFit: Scavenging means both clearing exhaust from an engine cylinder and searching through refuse for food.

clue.text: Yank is a fool

explanation.definitionFit: A jerk is a sudden pull, and also slang for an idiot.

clue.text: Where people can plainly be seen to be giving a favourable impression

definitions.text: Where people can plainly be seen

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means presented favourably, and literally describes being well illuminated so clearly visible.

clue.text: Don't start the season by giving up prayer

indicators.note: an instruction to drop the opening letter of the next word's synonym

parts.note: winter is a season
cession is the ceding or giving up of rights or territory

explanation.surface: A plea not to open the sporting season by surrendering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start' removes the W from WINTER, leaving INTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercession is prayer offered on behalf of other people.

clue.text: Tried to be kind to the audience

indicators.note: what an audience hears, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Someone attempted to be nice to the people watching.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent SORT and SOUGHT sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Sought is the past tense of seek, meaning attempted.

clue.text: Betraying an informer

definitions.meaning: revealing, giving away, as a revealing sign does
a sneak who tells on others

explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign betrays a secret, and a telltale is a sneak who reports others.

clue.text: The way I escaped being killed

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
fled means ran away, escaped

explanation.surface: A survivor's account of how they got away from a deadly attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Stifled means smothered or suffocated, so put to death.

clue.text: Go away from the heart of Somerset for thrills

indicators.note: the letters lie within the middle of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Leave the middle of a quiet county in search of excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is a rural county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To set forth is to set out, depart on a journey.

clue.text: The grass is short here, giving reasonable access

parts.note: fair means reasonable, just
a way is a means of access or route

explanation.surface: A lawn kept mown, with a decent path to it.
explanation.walkthrough: On a golf course, the short-cut grass between tee and green is this.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course, the closely mown strip leading to the green.

clue.text: Approximation usually made from 16

definitions.meaning: something coming close to the real thing
in golf, the shot to the green is normally played from the fairway

explanation.definitionFit: An approach is a near likeness, and in golf the shot played towards the green.

clue.text: Truthful article about a priest

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
c stands for circa, about
a curate is an assistant priest

explanation.surface: An honest newspaper piece about a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate means correct, true to the facts.

clue.text: It's the end of the month — relax!

parts.note: Dec is short for December
to ease is to relax

explanation.surface: Month-end at last, time to unwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the end of the month' looks like one phrase but splits after 'end'.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is death, the end of life.

clue.text: Stick to the French class

parts.note: le is French for the
a rate is a class or grade, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Keep going with your French lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick something is to put up with or endure it.

clue.text: A rendezvous for 17

parts.note: a rendezvous is a meeting place, a venue

explanation.surface: A meeting place for the approach.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way of approaching something, literally a tree-lined approach road.

clue.text: First appearance in prison? Make contact with advocate

indicators.note: the opening letter that shows up in the word that follows

parts.note: to reach someone is to get in touch with them

explanation.surface: A new inmate tries to get in touch with a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advocate' looks like a lawyer but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To preach is to urge or recommend something earnestly.

clue.text: Working pros, sure to be unruly

indicators.note: working the letters over rearranges them

explanation.surface: Professionals on the job are bound to be rowdy.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstreperous means noisy and hard to control.

clue.text: Forward succeeded in front of goal

indicators.note: places the first letter before the next piece

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A striker scores having got in front of the net.
explanation.definitionFit: To forward a letter is to send it on.

clue.text: Russian leader getting out of bed

indicators.note: the first letter leaves the word for bed

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed

explanation.surface: A Soviet ruler rising in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian leader' wants to be the definition; 'leader' is part of the deletion, removing D from DIVAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name, used for a Russian in general.

clue.text: West End workers keep strange pets

indicators.note: the final letter of the word before
the workers hold the word for strange within them

parts.note: worker ants are crossword's standard workers
rum means odd, strange

explanation.surface: Theatreland staff keep some odd animals.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre district. 'West End' gives T, the end of West.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is an old word for a fit of sulking or bad temper.

clue.text: In the denouement, each new novel could be improved

indicators.note: the scrambled letters sit within the word for denouement

parts.note: the denouement is the end of a story

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: A novel's ending could be made better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book in this literary surface but is the anagram signal; 'In' places the rearranged letters inside the word for a story's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Enhanced means made better or greater.
